report.summary: Chunk 3 of picker.py: work_queue_candidates validation, load_inventory, _head_sha, _queue_repo_path, and _load_work_queue_file. Claims about process spawning, git file reading, and fallback behavior are partially checkable.
risks: _head_sha | medium | Claims to read HEAD straight off disk without spawning git, but the chunk ends before showing the full implementation; the claim is only partially checkable. | Complete the function and verify no subprocess calls exist.

_head_sha | medium | Claim about 'test_there_is_no_apply_path_in_this_module' enforcing no process-spawning stdlib module is named in this file is uncheckable because the test is not in this chunk. | Locate the test and verify the assertion.

handoff.purpose: Define work queue validation, feature inventory loading, and HEAD sha resolution from git files.

symbols.name: _load_work_queue_file
symbols.note: Reads work queue JSON from a path, validates structure, returns data and detail dict.

symbols.name: _queue_repo_path
symbols.note: Validates and converts a repo-relative path string to a canonical posix path relative to resolved repo root.

symbols.name: work_queue_candidates
symbols.note: Validates an entire daedalus-work-queue/1 source, returns candidates, notes, and detail dict.

symbols.name: _read_text
symbols.note: Reads a file as UTF-8 text with error replacement, returns None on OSError.

symbols.name: _head_sha
symbols.note: Resolves HEAD sha by reading .git files directly, no subprocess.

claims.text: This module spawns no child process at all, and test_there_is_no_apply_path_in_this_module enforces that by asserting the process-spawning stdlib module is never so much as NAMED in this file
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the test function, and the claim about naming is not verifiable from this code alone.

claims.text: HEAD is resolved by reading git's own on-disk files.
claims.why: The chunk shows _head_sha reading .git as a directory or file, and the code does not import subprocess or similar.

claims.text: Handles the three shapes that occur here: .git as a directory (primary checkout), .git as a gitdir: pointer file (linked worktree, where refs live in the shared common dir), and a detached HEAD holding a raw sha.
claims.why: The chunk shows handling of .git as directory and as file (gitdir pointer), but the detached HEAD case and actual sha extraction are not shown; the function is incomplete in this chunk.

claims.text: Missing, unreadable, not JSON, or JSON that is not an object all degrade to an empty inventory.
claims.why: The code catches OSError, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError and returns {}; and checks isinstance(data, dict) else {}.

claims.text: The picker's job is to rank work, not to be the thing that breaks when a docs file is mid-edit -- and an empty queue is a truthful answer to 'what does this file tell us', where a traceback is not.
claims.why: The implementation returns {} on any error, fulfilling the described philosophy.

claims.text: Validation is whole-file and fail-closed: one malformed ready task makes the source invalid instead of silently shortening the operator's queue.
claims.why: The function raises WorkQueueInvalid on any malformed task, never skipping or continuing.

claims.text: Non-ready tasks are valid records but are not candidates.
claims.why: The code increments non_ready and continues without adding to candidates for non-ready states.

observations.what: work_queue_candidates uses _head_sha and _confined_path; the latter is not defined in this chunk.
_queue_repo_path calls _confined_path and then calls .relative_to(repo_root.resolve()), which could raise ValueError if the resolved path is not under repo_root.
_head_sha docstring claims to handle three shapes, but the chunk ends before the logic for reading the HEAD file or following gitdir pointers is complete.
The claim about test_there_is_no_apply_path_in_this_module is uncheckable; the test is not in this chunk.
